- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model underestimates upside — add 2–4% buffer to forecast mean.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) after a rally, model fails to reverse — apply mean reversion to 10–15% of recent 5-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 2–5 days — shift forecast up by 0.5–1.5% per day for lagged events.
- When multiple auction events occur in 7–14 days, model overestimates supply shock — reduce forecast by 1–3% per event if supply net is negative.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast mean.
